items.title: Welcome to FinAgent
items.text:
FinAgent is a local-first personal finance assistant for the bank statements you already download. It files your statements, categorizes transactions with rules and optional lookup/model tools, and turns the results into a private dashboard on your own machine.

No bank login is required. Your statement files, settings, rules, and processed results stay in folders you control.

Get running with Quick Start

items.title: Recognize the dashboard
items.text:
The documentation uses the same icons as FinAgent so each guide is easy to match to its page or control.

Icon Page or control Where to find it Overview Primary navigation Monthly Primary navigation Budget Primary navigation Transactions Primary navigation Import statements Top-right toolbar Process statements Top-right toolbar Configuration Top-right toolbar

items.title: Start here
items.text:
• Installing for the first time? Open Installation in the navigation and choose your platform, or use Quick Start.
  • Ready to add data? Import explains supported statement files, account labels, dates, and where each file goes.
  • Want to understand a run? Process walks through every stage and the controls that protect existing categories.
  • Choosing lookup or AI options? Begin with Settings, then use the focused Location Engine and AI Engine guides.

items.title: The everyday flow
items.text:
1. Configure FinAgent in Settings.
  2. Add one or more bank statements in Import.
  3. Start the workflow from Process.
  4. Explore Overview, Monthly, Transactions, and Budget.
  5. Correct a transaction or add a Rule when a merchant needs a better match.

The How to Use section in the navigation contains a page for each step and feature. For profiles, command-line runs, and maintenance tools, open Advanced Use.

Local by default

Ollama runs categorization on your machine. Optional map services and cloud models contact their named providers only when you select them; their pages explain exactly what is sent before you enable one.

items.title: AI Engine
items.text:
In FinAgent: Configuration Settings AI Engine for Categorization

The AI Engine is FinAgent's final categorization stage for transactions that Rules and the Location Engine could not resolve.

Rules -> Location Engine -> AI Engine -> Merge

It reads a merchant description, chooses from FinAgent's supported Categories, and returns a structured category. It does not calculate dashboard totals, modify raw statements, or replace protected manual choices.

items.title: Choose an option
items.text:
Provider Runs where Internet Cost Setup Ollama Your machine Not for categorization Free Install Ollama and pull a model OpenRouter Hosted API Required Complimentary or paid model-dependent usage Create an API key Claude Anthropic API Required Paid token usage Add billing and create an API key None Disabled No Free No installation

Choose Ollama when privacy and offline processing matter most. Choose OpenRouter for hosted models with a complimentary starting option. Choose Claude when you prefer Anthropic's models and accept paid API usage. Choose None for deterministic Rules and optional Location Engine only.

items.title: Ollama: local and private
items.text: Ollama runs models on your computer, so transaction descriptions do not leave the machine during AI categorization. Performance depends on available memory, CPU, and GPU resources.

items.title: Install Ollama
items.text:
macOSWindowsLinuxDocker

Download the app from ollama.com/download, or install it with Homebrew:

brew install ollama

Open the Ollama app, or start the service with ollama serve.

Download and run the Windows installer from ollama.com/download. Ollama normally starts as a background service after installation.

curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

If the service is not already running, start it with ollama serve.

Ollama is included in the FinAgent Docker image. Pull the small Docker default during startup:

./docker_up.sh --ollama-model \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

Supply a model name after --ollama-model to choose another one.

items.title: Pull and select a model
items.text:
For a native installation, pull a model before processing:

ollama pull qwen2.5:3b
ollama list

Then open Settings -> AI Engine for Categorization, choose Ollama, select the downloaded model, and use Test Ollama.

FinAgent's configured default is qwen2.5:3b. The Settings list also supports:

Model Practical use qwen2.5:0.5b Smallest option; useful on limited hardware or for quick tests qwen2.5:3b Balanced FinAgent default qwen2.5:7b Larger model with higher memory use llama3.2:3b Alternative compact general model mistral:7b Larger alternative with higher memory use phi3:mini Compact alternative

The dashboard can pull a missing model on native installations. Docker models must be selected with docker_up.sh --ollama-model [NAME] and persist in the ollama-data volume.

items.title: OpenRouter: hosted model access
items.text: OpenRouter requires no local model installation. It sends unresolved merchant descriptions to the selected hosted model.

items.title: Set up OpenRouter
items.text:
1. Create an account at openrouter.ai.
  2. Open openrouter.ai/keys.
  3. Create a key and copy it when shown.
  4. In Settings -> AI Engine for Categorization, choose OpenRouter.
  5. Paste the key, select a model, save, and use Test OpenRouter key.

FinAgent currently offers these Settings choices:

Model Notes inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash:free Default complimentary option nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free Complimentary large-model option nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free Complimentary speed-focused option

Complimentary models may be rate-limited, renamed, or temporarily unavailable by OpenRouter. Review the provider's model page before relying on one for an automated workflow.

items.title: Claude: Anthropic API
items.text: Claude requires no local model installation, but Anthropic API access is paid. FinAgent reports an estimated output-token cost after processing; the provider's billing page remains authoritative.

items.title: Set up Claude
items.text:
1. Create or open an account at console.anthropic.com.
  2. Add billing or API credits.
  3. Open API Keys, create a key, and copy it when shown.
  4. In Settings -> AI Engine for Categorization, choose Claude.
  5. Paste the key, select a model, save, and use Test Claude key.

Available Settings choices are:

Model Notes claude-haiku-4-5 Default; faster and lower cost claude-opus-4-5 Most capable option; higher cost

items.title: None: deterministic processing
items.text: Choose None - rules and location only when no AI provider should run. No AI software, model download, key, internet connection, or token billing is needed. Rules and the selected Location Engine continue to categorize transactions.

items.title: What cloud providers receive
items.text:
The AI Engine supplies the transaction description and the category vocabulary needed by the prompt. Cloud requests do not include transaction amounts, account numbers, raw statement files, or your display name. Transactions already resolved by Rules or the Location Engine normally skip this stage.

API keys are stored in your local profile configuration and returned to the dashboard only as masked values. Do not publish config.json or paste keys into commands that shell history may save.

items.title: Advanced settings
items.text:
The Advanced control in Settings exposes:

  • Temperature (0.1 by default): lower values make choices more repeatable.
  • Max tokens (4096 by default): limits each response.

The defaults are tuned for short, structured categorization output. Change them only when a selected model consistently fails to return a valid category.

items.title: Cache and one-run controls
items.text:
Repeated descriptions can use the active model's local cache. Advanced terminal commands can rebuild it or change the provider for one run:

finagent --clear-llm-cache --llm-provider ollama --orgs boa
finagent --refresh-llm-cache --llm-provider open_router --orgs boa
finagent --no-llm --orgs boa

See Running from the Terminal for every provider, cache, and batch option.

items.title: Protect and improve results
items.text:
Before a dashboard processing run, FinAgent asks whether prior manual, Location Engine, and AI Engine categories may be overwritten. Keep protections enabled when existing decisions should win.

Review AI results on Transactions. Correct a one-time exception manually, or create a deterministic Rule for a merchant you expect to see again. That rule will run before both engines on future imports.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• Ollama not reachable: open the Ollama app or run ollama serve, then use Re-check in Settings.
  • Ollama model missing: run ollama pull <model> or use the dashboard's native Pull model action.
  • OpenRouter or Claude test fails: verify the key, selected model, internet access, provider balance, and rate limits.
  • No AI categories appear: confirm the provider is not None and remember that Rules and Location Engine matches intentionally skip AI processing.

items.title: Categories
items.text:
In FinAgent: Configuration Categories

FinAgent uses a two-level category vocabulary written as group:subcategory, for example food:groceries or housing:rent_mortgage. The dashboard displays friendly labels and emojis, while the stable value keeps rules, lookup results, model prompts, budgets, and historical data aligned.

items.title: How categorization works
items.text:
Every processing stage chooses from the same vocabulary:

  1. Rules apply deterministic merchant keywords.
  2. The Location Engine maps supported business types.
  3. The optional AI Engine selects from the remaining valid categories.
  4. A manual edit on Transactions records your choice as user_defined.

The Transactions page shows how each result was assigned. Categories left unresolved remain uncategorized instead of being forced into a weak match.

items.title: Browse available categories
items.text:
Open Configuration -> Categories in the dashboard. The page groups all built-in values by their top-level group and provides the exact identifiers used by Rules and processing. Use search to find the closest supported option before creating a new one.

The shipped vocabulary covers income, housing, food, transport, shopping, health, financial activity, transfers, entertainment, travel, charity, and other common personal-finance activity. The application itself is the current reference list, so it stays synchronized with the installed release.

items.title: Adding a category
items.text:
Adding categories is intentionally limited to the Dev profile. The built-in set is tuned across rules, lookup mappings, model prompts, analytics, and budget matching; unnecessary additions fragment reporting history.

When a genuinely new category is needed:

  • Choose an existing top-level group.
  • Enter a subcategory; FinAgent converts it to lower_snake_case.
  • Optionally choose an emoji for dashboard display.
  • Save it, then update the relevant rule or transaction.

A newly added category applies to future choices and processing. It does not silently rewrite old transactions. Reprocess deliberately if historical rows should use it.

items.title: Manual corrections
items.text: Use the edit action on the Transactions page to change one row. FinAgent marks the result user_defined; normal processing protects that choice during the merge. For a repeated merchant pattern, create a Rule instead so future imports receive the same category automatically.

items.title: Import
items.text:
In FinAgent: Top-right toolbar -> Import statements

Import brings downloaded bank statements into FinAgent's statements folder. It does not process or categorize them yet; it validates the form, gives the file a consistent name, and places it in the correct bank/account folder for the next run.

Before importing, complete Settings. New users reach Import automatically after selecting Complete setup.

Use transaction exports, not PDFs

Download CSV, comma-separated, or a supported tabular text export from your bank. PDF statements are visual documents and are not supported. Bank of America checking .txt exports are converted automatically.

items.title: Supported institutions
items.text: Institution Account types Import folder American Express Credit AMEX/CreditAC Bank of America Checking, Credit BOA/CheckingAC or BOA/CreditAC Chase Checking, Credit CHASE/CheckingAC or CHASE/CreditAC Citi Credit CITI/CreditAC US Bank Checking, Credit USBANK/CheckingAC or USBANK/CreditAC

items.title: Import a statement
items.text:
1. Export transactions from the bank website in a supported format.
  2. Select Import statements in the top-right dashboard tools.
  3. Choose the institution and account type.
  4. Enter the account's last four digits.
  5. Optionally enter an alphanumeric account label.
  6. Optionally enter both statement dates in YYYYMMDD format.
  7. Choose the downloaded file and select Import.

Repeat these steps for every statement you want included, then select Run processing to continue to Process.

items.title: Account status
items.text: Each linked account shows a Processed or Draft badge. Draft means the account's imported statement has not been found in your merged dashboard data yet; Processed means it has. This is a live check against the dashboard's merged transaction history each time the Import page loads, so the badge stays correct even if a manual reset or edit changes what's actually on the dashboard, not just what was clicked "Import" once. The date range shown under a Processed account reflects the earliest and latest transaction dates actually found for it, not the dates typed in during import.

items.title: Account labels
items.text: Labels make multiple accounts from the same institution easier to recognize. FinAgent remembers a label for the matching institution, account type, and last four digits. If the label is blank, it reuses a known match or creates a unique five-digit label.

items.title: Statement dates
items.text:
Dates are optional, but supply both when using them. For example, January 1 through March 31, 2026 is 20260101 through 20260331.

When both fields are blank, FinAgent assigns a safe synthetic range beginning at 19000101. Later undated imports for that account continue after the previous synthetic end date so their filenames do not collide. These filename dates identify files; processing still reads transaction dates from the statement contents.

items.title: What FinAgent stores
items.text:
An imported filename records the institution, account label, account type, last four digits, and date range. The original upload is copied into your configured statements directory; processing output stays in the separate processing directory.

FinAgent also stores reusable account metadata in statement_accounts.json inside the statements folder. This local file keeps labels and automatic date ranges consistent.

items.title: Importing by hand
items.text: Advanced users can place supported files directly into a matching folder such as <statements>/BOA/CheckingAC/. Use the same naming pattern as existing files so account and date metadata can be parsed reliably. The dashboard Import page is recommended because it validates and names the file for you.

items.title: Duplicate and corrected statements
items.text:
Import does not delete earlier files. If a bank issues a corrected export, remove or archive the superseded statement from the statements folder before processing to avoid duplicate source rows.

When all files are ready, use Process. Platform-specific folder and permission notes are under Installation in the navigation.

items.title: Install with Docker
items.text: The Docker release contains the packaged FinAgent binary, dashboard, documentation, Node.js runtime, and Ollama. It does not publish the private source tree or raw Python source files.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Docker Desktop, or Docker Engine with Docker Compose.
  • FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz from the latest release.
  • docker_up.sh and docker-compose.yml from the public repository.
  • One host folder for statements and one for processing output.

items.title: Load and start
items.text:
Keep the three downloaded files in one folder, then run:

docker load -i FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz
chmod +x docker_up.sh

./docker_up.sh \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing" \
  --no-ollama-model

Open the dashboard at http://localhost:3001 and the local documentation at http://localhost:3003. Missing host folders are created automatically. Their paths appear locked in Settings because changing a bind mount requires recreating the container.

Preview first

Add --dry-run to print the Compose command, ports, mounts, provider, and model choice without starting a container.

items.title: Ports
items.text:
The dashboard defaults to host port 3001; documentation defaults to the dashboard port plus 2. Set either explicitly:

./docker_up.sh \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing" \
  --port 4100 \
  --docs-port 4200 \
  --no-ollama-model

Ports must be different whole numbers from 1024 through 65535. Keep the dashboard port at 65533 or lower because FinAgent reserves adjacent internal ports.

items.title: Ollama models
items.text:
Ollama is installed in the image. Downloads are optional and persist in the ollama-data volume.

# Pull and select qwen2.5:0.5b
./docker_up.sh --ollama-model \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

# Pull and select another model
./docker_up.sh --ollama-model qwen2.5:3b \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

With neither model flag, an interactive launch asks whether to download the small default. An unattended launch does not prompt. Use --no-ollama-model to skip downloading explicitly.

items.title: Claude and OpenRouter
items.text:
Keep cloud keys out of shell history by using a local permission-restricted environment file.

ClaudeOpenRouter 
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/finagent"
printf '%s\n' 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your-key' > "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env"
chmod 600 "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env"

./docker_up.sh --llm-provider claude \
  --env-file "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env" \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/finagent"
printf '%s\n' 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=your-key' > "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env"
chmod 600 "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env"

./docker_up.sh --llm-provider open_router \
  --env-file "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env" \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

The env file accepts ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Keys are injected at startup, masked in the dashboard, and never copied into the image.

items.title: Persistent data
items.text:
Data Storage Survives recreation Imported statements Host --statements folder Yes Processing and dashboard data Host --processing folder Yes FinAgent settings Host --config folder, default .docker-config Yes Ollama models Docker volume ollama-data Yes

After setup, use Import and Process exactly as in a native installation.

items.title: Check, restart, and stop
items.text:
docker ps --filter name=finagent
docker logs finagent
curl http://localhost:3001/api/health

docker restart finagent
docker compose --project-name finagent down

Run ./docker_up.sh again to recreate a stopped container with the mounts, ports, and provider options you want.

items.title: Update
items.text:
1. Download the new image archive and current launcher files.
  2. Run docker compose --project-name finagent down.
  3. Run docker load -i FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz.
  4. Start again with your normal ./docker_up.sh options.

Mounted data, configuration, and Ollama models remain available.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• Invalid port: choose distinct values in the documented range.
  • Cloud key missing: provide the key with --env-file or save it in Settings.
  • Ollama model unavailable: restart with --ollama-model or --ollama-model <name>.
  • Image not loaded: run docker load -i FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz.
  • All Docker launcher options: run ./docker_up.sh --help.

items.title: Install on Linux
items.text: The Linux x86_64 archive contains the packaged FinAgent binary and dashboard runtime. Normal use does not require a separate Python or Node.js installation.

items.title: Download and install
items.text:
1. Download FinAgent-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz.

  2. Extract the archive:

    tar -xzf FinAgent-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd finagent_bundle

  3. Run the included installer. It installs to your user account, adds the finagent command, and creates an application-menu entry without sudo:

    ./install.sh

  4. Start FinAgent from the app menu or terminal:

    finagent

To run the bundle in place instead, mark the executable if needed and launch it directly:

chmod +x ./finagent
./finagent

items.title: Desktop integration notes
items.text: A browser must be available for the dashboard. On minimal or remote Linux systems, start FinAgent and open the printed http://localhost:<port> address from a browser that can reach the same machine.

items.title: Next steps
items.text: The first launch opens Settings. Complete it, Import a bank CSV or supported tabular text statement, then use Process. For automation and maintenance options, see Running from the Terminal.

items.title: Install on macOS
items.text: The macOS release includes FinAgent and its dashboard runtime. Python and Node.js do not need to be installed separately.

items.title: Download and install
items.text:
1. Download FinAgent-macOS.dmg from the latest release.
  2. Open the DMG.
  3. Drag FinAgent.app into Applications.
  4. Open FinAgent from Applications.

items.title: Approve the first launch
items.text:
FinAgent development releases are not notarized with a paid Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may block the first launch after each install or update.

Try these options in order:

  1. Control-click FinAgent.app, select Open, then select Open again.
  2. If macOS still blocks it, open System Settings -> Privacy & Security, find the FinAgent message, select Open Anyway, and authenticate.
  3. For a release downloaded from the official FinAgent repository that you trust, remove the quarantine flag in Terminal:
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/FinAgent.app

Double-clicking the app opens a Terminal window for its local process and then opens the dashboard in your browser. Keep that Terminal window open while using FinAgent.

items.title: Optional terminal command
items.text:
Add an alias when you want to use the advanced command-line workflow:

zshbash 
echo 'alias finagent="/Applications/FinAgent.app/Contents/MacOS/finagent"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

echo 'alias finagent="/Applications/FinAgent.app/Contents/MacOS/finagent"' >> ~/.bash_profile
source ~/.bash_profile

Verify it:

finagent --version

items.title: Next steps
items.text: Complete Settings, Import a bank CSV or supported tabular text statement, then use Process. See Restarting FinAgent for clean shutdown and relaunch options.

items.title: Install on Windows
items.text: The Windows x64 installer includes FinAgent and its dashboard runtime. Python and Node.js do not need to be installed separately.

items.title: Download and install
items.text:
1. Download FinAgent-Windows-x64.exe.
  2. Run the installer.
  3. If Microsoft Defender SmartScreen appears, select More info, verify that the file came from the official FinAgent release, then select Run anyway.
  4. Keep Launch FinAgent selected on the final installer page.

The installer creates a Start Menu shortcut and can create a desktop shortcut. Use either one for later launches.

items.title: Diagnostics
items.text: If installation fails unexpectedly, FinAgent writes a short redacted diagnostic report in the Windows temporary folder and opens a pre-filled GitHub issue for your review. It contains version and failure information, not configuration contents, environment variables, bank data, or API keys. Attach an installer log only when a maintainer requests it.

items.title: Next steps
items.text: The first launch opens Settings. Complete it, Import a bank CSV or supported tabular text statement, then use Process. PowerShell commands and maintenance options are in Running from the Terminal.

items.title: Location Engine
items.text:
In FinAgent: Configuration Settings Location Engine for Categorization

The Location Engine turns an unclear statement description into a likely business type before FinAgent asks the AI Engine. It runs as part of processing, and most methods contact an external map service directly from your machine.

Rules -> Location Engine -> AI Engine -> Merge

Select a method in Settings -> Location Engine for Categorization. Accepted results are cached in your local processing folder, making repeat runs faster and reducing network requests.

items.title: Choose a method
items.text:
Settings option Config value Profile Internet Direct cost Best for Open Street Map nominatim Personal, Dev Required Free Simple, no-key lookup Place API place_api Personal, Dev Required Google billing Maximum Google coverage Place API combined flow place_api_combined Personal, Dev Required Google billing on fallback Fewer paid Google calls Disabled none Personal, Dev No Free Rules and optional AI only

For most users, start with Open Street Map. Choose Place API combined flow when free results leave too many merchants unresolved. Choose Disabled when no merchant text should be sent to a map provider.

items.title: Open Street Map
items.text: Open Street Map uses the public Nominatim service. It requires no API key. FinAgent sends the merchant description and available location text, accepts only usable category evidence, and stores an accepted result locally.

items.title: Set it up
items.text:
1. Open Settings -> Location Engine for Categorization.
  2. Choose Open Street Map (free, built in).
  3. Optionally open Advanced and enable the contact-email field. Sharing an email with OpenStreetMap is voluntary and off by default.
  4. Save, then run Process.

Use this option when you want free lookup with minimal setup. Public Nominatim may rate-limit heavy usage, so keep the local cache and avoid unnecessary refreshes.

items.title: Google Places API
items.text: Google Places is FinAgent's higher-coverage location option. It does not require Selenium or a browser driver, but it requires a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.

items.title: Place API modes
items.text:
• Place API queries Google for each unresolved, uncached merchant. It offers the most direct Google coverage and usually makes the most paid requests.
  • Place API combined flow tries free OpenStreetMap first and calls Google only when OpenStreetMap has no usable category. Start here when cost matters.

Each mode keeps a separate local cache.

items.title: Create and protect an API key
items.text:
1. Open Google Cloud Console.
  2. Create or select a project with billing enabled.
  3. Enable Places API (New).
  4. Create an API key.
  5. Restrict the key to Places API (New) and add appropriate application restrictions for your environment.
  6. In FinAgent, open Settings -> Location Engine for Categorization.
  7. Choose Place API or Place API combined flow.
  8. Paste the key into Google Places API key, save, then run Process.

Google maintains the current walkthrough at Get a Places API key. FinAgent masks a saved key when the dashboard reads it back. Do not publish your config.json or include the key in screenshots.

items.title: How a Google match is accepted
items.text:
For each unresolved merchant not already cached, FinAgent:

  1. Extracts a merchant query and the most specific available location hint.
  2. Sends that query directly from your machine to Google Places.
  3. Compares the returned business name with statement evidence.
  4. Requires an exact ZIP match when ZIP evidence exists, or compatible city/state evidence when that is the best available location.
  5. Maps only specific supported Google place types to a FinAgent category.
  6. Caches an accepted category for later runs.

Broad types such as store and point_of_interest are ignored because they do not identify a useful category. Errors, ambiguous names, location mismatches, and unmapped types remain unresolved instead of being guessed.

items.title: Privacy and cost
items.text:
Google receives the merchant query and available ZIP, city, or state needed for the search. FinAgent does not include transaction amounts, account numbers, raw statement files, or your display name. Requests go directly to Google; there is no FinAgent proxy.

Google bills the Cloud project attached to your key. FinAgent adds no fee and cannot determine the final invoice. To control usage:

  • Prefer Place API combined flow.
  • Keep cached results instead of clearing them routinely.
  • Restrict and monitor the API key in Google Cloud.
  • Configure Google Cloud quotas and billing alerts.
  • Review current Places API pricing.

items.title: Disabled
items.text: Choose Disabled to skip the Location Engine. No merchant description is sent to OpenStreetMap or Google. Rules still run, followed by the selected AI Engine, if enabled.

items.title: How FinAgent treats every result
items.text: Location evidence is never permission to guess. Every resolver compares merchant and location evidence, maps only recognized business types, and leaves uncertain results uncategorized. An unresolved transaction continues to the AI Engine or remains available for manual review.

items.title: Cache controls
items.text:
Normal runs reuse the active method's local cache. Advanced terminal runs can clear or refresh it:

finagent --clear-lookup-cache --orgs boa
finagent --refresh-lookup-cache --orgs boa

Use refresh only when a cached business is outdated or while testing a resolver; it intentionally makes new network requests. See Settings for all configuration fields and Running from the Terminal for one-run method overrides.

items.title: Process
items.text:
In FinAgent: Top-right toolbar -> Process statements

Process runs the complete FinAgent workflow and refreshes dashboard data. It starts with the statements collected by Import, applies the tools selected in Settings, and merges the result into one persistent transaction master.

items.title: Before a run
items.text:
Confirm that:

  • Setup is complete and at least one supported statement is present.
  • The Settings page shows the model and location method you intend to use.
  • Any required local service, such as Ollama, is running.
  • Cloud API keys have passed the Settings test when using a cloud provider.

Select Process statements in the top-right dashboard tools.

items.title: Run from the dashboard
items.text:
1. Review Run defaults. These show the active Location Engine and AI Engine.
  2. Leave the date fields blank to process all available statement data, or choose an inclusive From and To range.
  3. Review the merge protection options.
  4. Select Run processing.
  5. Watch overall progress and the location/model sub-progress bars. Expand the run log for detailed output.
  6. When the run completes, return to Overview or Transactions to review it.

The date picker is not limited to the range from a previous run. A selected range controls the run and dashboard view without deleting older rows from the persistent transaction master.

items.title: Merge protection
items.text:
FinAgent carries existing categorized rows into a normal refresh. Before a run, you can independently allow replacement of:

  • Manual categories (user_defined)
  • AI model categories (llm:<provider>)
  • Location categories (location_lookup)

Leave a protection off when those prior choices should win. Enable an overwrite only when you deliberately want that stage recalculated. Rebuilding with --overwrite-dashboard-data is a separate terminal maintenance operation that replaces the dashboard master from current pipeline output.

items.title: 1. Discover and parse statements
items.text: FinAgent scans the configured institution/account folders, identifies supported exports, and converts each bank's columns into a common transaction shape. Bank of America tabular checking exports are converted as part of import.

items.title: 2. Normalize transactions
items.text: Dates, descriptions, signs, account metadata, and duplicate evidence are normalized. Optional organization and date filters are applied for the run.

items.title: 3. Apply Rules
items.text: The deterministic Rules engine checks transaction descriptions first. Rule matches are fast, repeatable, and marked with stage rule.

items.title: 4. Run the Location Engine
items.text: Unresolved merchants go to the configured Location Engine method. Accepted results are marked location_lookup; uncertain results move on without a forced category.

items.title: 5. Run the AI Engine
items.text: Still-unresolved transactions go to the selected AI Engine. Ollama runs locally; OpenRouter and Claude use their APIs. Results record the provider, for example llm:ollama or llm:claude.

items.title: 6. Merge protected decisions
items.text: FinAgent compares the new output with the dashboard's persistent master and preserves prior manual, model, and location decisions according to the run's merge choices. Carried rows may use the merge stage.

items.title: 7. Publish dashboard data
items.text: The latest authoritative transactions are merged into dashboard_data/master_transactions.csv. Dashboard summaries are calculated from that master and the selected inclusive view range. Refresh the browser if a completed run is not immediately visible.

items.title: Categorization stages in the dashboard
items.text: Stage Meaning rule A deterministic keyword rule matched. location_lookup A configured map/location resolver supplied the category. llm:<provider> The selected model supplied the category. user_defined You edited the category on Transactions. merge A protected value was carried from an earlier run. uncategorized No stage had enough evidence.

items.title: Progress, logs, and cost
items.text: The page shows overall progress plus dedicated location and model progress. The collapsible log is the best place to identify the current institution, stage, or error. For Claude runs, FinAgent reports observed output tokens and an estimated USD cost; Anthropic billing remains authoritative.

items.title: When a run does not complete
items.text:
• No statements: return to Import.
  • No transactions produced: verify statement format and selected dates.
  • Lookup failures: confirm internet access and the selected method; cached or unresolved merchants can still continue to later stages.
  • Model failures: use the provider test in Settings and verify the selected model or API key.
  • Wrong category preserved: rerun with the relevant merge overwrite enabled, or correct the row manually.

Advanced organization filters, cache maintenance, non-interactive runs, and master-data maintenance are documented in Running from the Terminal.

items.title: Profiles
items.text:
In FinAgent: Configuration Settings Profile selector

Profiles keep everyday personal settings separate from development and testing settings. The active profile appears in the dashboard header.

items.title: Personal
items.text:
Personal is the default and the right choice for normal use.

  • Uses ~/.finagent/config.json by default.
  • Offers OpenStreetMap, Google Places, Google Places combined flow, or Off for the Location Engine.
  • Supports Ollama, OpenRouter, Claude, or no AI Engine.
  • Keeps Selenium maintenance options hidden.
  • Prevents adding categories outside the shipped vocabulary.

items.title: Dev
items.text:
Dev is intended for maintainers and controlled experiments.

  • Uses ~/.finagent-dev/config.json by default.
  • Keeps its own folders, provider, keys, lookup method, and dashboard settings.
  • Adds Google Maps Selenium and OpenStreetMap/Selenium Combined lookup.
  • Exposes an optional ChromeDriver path.
  • Allows adding custom categories, although using the built-in set is still recommended.

items.title: Switch in Settings
items.text:
1. Open Configuration -> Settings.
  2. Select Dev and enter the application password (finagent), or select Personal to return.
  3. Review the newly displayed profile's values and config path.
  4. Select Save changes to activate it.

Changing the toggle previews the other profile; it does not activate that profile until save. Discard returns to the currently active profile. Processing always uses the active profile.

Read Settings for every configuration section and required field.

items.title: Start with a profile from the terminal
items.text:
finagent --profile personal
finagent --profile dev

Without --profile, FinAgent starts Personal. The profile flag is consumed before configuration loads, so it also works with processing and maintenance commands:

finagent --profile dev --orgs boa
finagent --profile personal --dashboard-only

items.title: Custom development paths
items.text:
The development helper dashboard/restart-server.sh accepts profile and config path overrides. When it starts with --profile and --config-dir, that custom config directory remains attached to the starting profile while the server is running. The other profile keeps its normal config path.

An explicit --data-dir is pinned for that development launch. Without it, activating a profile also changes statements and processing paths to those in the selected profile.

For all launch flags, see Running from the Terminal.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text: Pick a platform. Install, open Settings, then Import and Process.

items.title: macOS
items.text:
1. Download FinAgent-macOS.dmg.
  2. Drag FinAgent.app to Applications.
  3. Control-click the app and choose Open on first launch.

macOS details

items.title: Linux x86_64
items.text:
tar -xzf FinAgent-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd finagent_bundle
./install.sh
finagent

Linux details

items.title: Windows x64
items.text:
Start-Process .\FinAgent-Windows-x64.exe

Keep Launch FinAgent selected.

Windows details

items.title: Docker
items.text:
docker load -i FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz
chmod +x docker_up.sh
./docker_up.sh \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing" \
  --no-ollama-model

Dashboard: localhost:3001 Docs: localhost:3003

Docker details

items.title: Then
items.text:
Settings -> Import -> Process

No bank statement handy yet? Download the demo statement from the public repository and import it to try the full dashboard with sample data.

items.title: Restarting FinAgent
items.text:
Related setting: Configuration Settings Dashboard

Restart FinAgent after changing the dashboard port or when a local service must be started with a new environment. Model and location selections usually need a new Process run, not an application restart.

items.title: macOS app or native binary
items.text:
1. Stop FinAgent by pressing ++ctrl+c++ in the Terminal window it opened, or close that window. On macOS, you can also quit FinAgent from the Dock.
  2. Open FinAgent again from Applications, the Start Menu, desktop shortcut, or your platform's normal launcher.
  3. Use the new dashboard address if you changed the port.

A normal relaunch opens the existing dashboard data without automatically processing statements.

items.title: Terminal
items.text:
Stop the active process with ++ctrl+c++, then run:

finagent

To state the dashboard-only behavior explicitly:

finagent --dashboard-only

Use finagent --profile dev when the Dev profile should be active at startup. See Running from the Terminal for every option.

items.title: Docker
items.text:
Restart the current container without changing mounts or settings:

docker restart finagent

To change ports, mounted folders, startup provider, or model, recreate it:

docker compose --project-name finagent down
./docker_up.sh \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing" \
  --no-ollama-model

Statements, processing output, configuration, and downloaded Ollama models remain in their host folders or named volume. See Docker Installation for all startup options.

items.title: Port already in use
items.text:
An earlier process may still own the configured port. On macOS or Linux:

lsof -i tcp:3001
kill <PID>

Replace 3001 with the configured dashboard port and stop only the process you recognize as the old FinAgent instance.

items.title: Dashboard looks stale
items.text: Wait for Process to report completion, then hard-refresh the browser (++cmd+shift+r++ on macOS or ++ctrl+shift+r++ on Windows/Linux). A normal restart does not rerun processing.

items.title: Folder paths need to change
items.text:
Native folder paths are locked after initial setup. Stop FinAgent and run:

finagent --reconfigure

For Docker, recreate the container with new --statements and --processing mounts instead.

items.title: Rules
items.text:
In FinAgent: Configuration Rule Engine

Rules are deterministic keyword checks that run first in every processing run. They are fast, repeatable, and do not require internet access.

A rule connects one or more transaction-description keywords to a category. When the evidence matches, FinAgent assigns that category and records rule as the categorization stage. Transactions without a match continue to the Location Engine, then the optional AI Engine.

items.title: Rule priority
items.text:
Rules are evaluated by priority. More specific merchant patterns should run before broad terms so a generic keyword does not capture the transaction first. Built-in rules occupy the lower priority range; custom dashboard rules must use priority 52 or higher and may use decimals.

When two rules could match, inspect their keyword coverage and give the more specific one the earlier effective priority. Reprocess after changing rules to apply them to pipeline output.

items.title: Manage rules in the dashboard
items.text:
Open Configuration -> Rule Engine from the header menu. You can:

  • Search and filter built-in or custom rules.
  • Review keywords before opening a rule.
  • Add a custom rule with a unique name, supported category, keywords, and priority.
  • Edit or delete rules you created.
  • Inspect built-in rules while keeping the shipped defaults intact.

Custom rules are stored locally and survive application updates. The editor validates names, priorities, required categories, and duplicate rules before saving.

items.title: Writing useful rules
items.text:
Prefer evidence that is stable in downloaded statements:

  • Use a merchant token such as TRADER JOE instead of a city or card suffix.
  • Add only variants that belong to the same merchant and category.
  • Avoid broad words such as PAYMENT, STORE, or a state abbreviation.
  • Choose an existing category whenever possible so reporting stays consistent.

items.title: Suggested workflow
items.text:
1. Review Uncategorized transactions on the Transactions page.
  2. Confirm that the same description pattern appears more than once.
  3. Add a focused rule for that pattern.
  4. Go to Process and run again.
  5. Verify the result and stage on Transactions.

For a one-time exception, edit the transaction directly instead. Manual edits are recorded as user_defined and protected by default during later merges.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
In FinAgent: Configuration Settings

Settings is where you tell FinAgent where your files live and which tools it may use while categorizing transactions. Everything is stored in a local config.json; there is no FinAgent account and no hosted settings service.

On a first launch, Settings also acts as the setup guide. Complete the required fields marked with *, then select Complete setup. FinAgent opens Import next.

items.title: First-run checklist
items.text:
1. Choose a statements folder and a processing folder.
  2. Enter the name FinAgent should use in greetings.
  3. Choose a Location Engine method.
  4. Choose an AI Engine provider, or select None.
  5. Confirm the dashboard port.
  6. Select Complete setup.

After setup, Import unlocks. Process unlocks when at least one supported statement is present, and the analysis pages unlock after a successful run.

State Pages available Setup not complete Settings Setup complete, no statements Settings, Import Statements available, no processed data Settings, Import, Process Processed dashboard data available All pages

items.title: Profile
items.text:
The profile switch chooses between Personal and Dev settings. Personal is the normal, privacy-focused experience. Dev uses a separate config file and unlocks maintainer options such as Selenium-based Google Maps lookup and adding categories.

Switching to Dev requires the password shown by the application. The selected profile is only a preview until you select Save changes. Learn how the two configurations stay isolated in Profiles.

items.title: Folders
items.text:
The two folders are selected during first-run setup:

  • Statements folder: stores imported bank CSV files and supported Bank of America tabular text exports. FinAgent creates bank and account-type subfolders as needed.
  • Processing folder: stores normalized transactions, categorized output, local caches, budgets, and the dashboard's persistent transaction data.

These paths are locked in the dashboard after setup. To move them safely, run:

finagent --reconfigure

In Docker, these paths are bind mounts and remain locked. Change them in the next docker_up.sh command when recreating the container. See Import for the statement filing workflow.

items.title: Identity
items.text: Your name is used for local greetings in FinAgent. It is never sent to a lookup service or model provider.

items.title: Dashboard
items.text:
Port controls the local dashboard address and defaults to 3001. Native runs listen on 127.0.0.1, so the dashboard is available only on your machine. Documentation normally uses the dashboard port plus 2.

A port change is saved immediately but takes effect on the next launch. Follow Restarting FinAgent after changing it.

items.title: Location Engine for Categorization
items.text:
The Location Engine runs after Rules and before the AI Engine. Choose one method:

  • Open Street Map: free Nominatim lookup; no API key required.
  • Place API: Google Places lookup for every unresolved merchant; billing-enabled API key required.
  • Place API combined flow: tries OpenStreetMap first and calls Google only when no useful category is found.
  • Off: sends no merchant description to a location service.
  • Google Maps and Combined: Dev-only Selenium methods that control a local Chrome browser.

The Advanced menu contains an optional OpenStreetMap contact email and, for Dev Selenium methods, a ChromeDriver path. Setup instructions, comparison guidance, Google Places key creation, privacy, and cost details are all in Location Engine.

items.title: AI Engine for Categorization
items.text:
The AI Engine only receives transactions that Rules and the Location Engine did not resolve. Available providers are:

  • Ollama: local and free. Select a model already downloaded on this machine, or use Pull model in native mode.
  • OpenRouter: hosted API. Add an OpenRouter key and choose one of the listed models; complimentary models may be rate-limited.
  • Claude: hosted Anthropic API. Add a billed API key and choose a model.
  • None: use deterministic Rules and the optional Location Engine only.

Use the provider's Test button before processing. API keys are stored in your local config and returned to the dashboard only as masked values. Ollama keeps merchant descriptions local. Cloud models receive merchant descriptions, not transaction amounts or account numbers.

The Advanced menu contains:

  • Temperature: randomness of model output, from 0 to 2; default 0.1.
  • Max tokens: response limit for each model call; default 4096.

The defaults are designed for FinAgent's structured prompt. See AI Engine before changing them.

items.title: Save, discard, and apply
items.text:
• Save changes writes the displayed profile and activates it.
  • Discard reloads the active profile and removes unsaved edits.
  • Complete setup writes the initial configuration and opens Import.

Most provider and lookup changes are used on the next processing run. After saving, go to Process and run again. Port changes require a restart.

items.title: Configuration reference
items.text:
Personal settings normally live at ~/.finagent/config.json; Dev settings normally live at ~/.finagent-dev/config.json. FINAGENT_CONFIG_DIR can supply a different directory for an advanced launch.

Key Values / default Purpose user_name empty Local display name. statements_dir ~/Documents/FinAgent/statements Raw imported statements; editable during setup or reconfiguration. processing_dir ~/Documents/FinAgent/processing Processed output, caches, budgets, and dashboard data. dashboard_port 3001 Dashboard port; documentation normally uses port + 2. ui_profile personal or dev Profile recorded in this config. llm_provider ollama, open_router, claude, or none AI categorization provider. ollama_model qwen2.5:3b Ollama model tag. ollama_api_url http://localhost:11434 Ollama server URL. openrouter_api_key empty OpenRouter secret, masked in the dashboard. openrouter_model inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash:free OpenRouter model. claude_api_key empty Anthropic secret, masked in the dashboard. claude_model claude-haiku-4-5 Claude model. temperature 0.1 Model randomness, from 0 to 2. max_tokens 4096 Maximum response tokens per model request. location_lookup_method nominatim Active lookup method. google_places_api_key empty Secret required for both Place API methods. nominatim_email empty Optional contact email sent to OpenStreetMap. google_maps_chromedriver_path empty Optional Dev-only Selenium driver path. setup_complete false initially Set automatically after first-run setup.

Do not publish config.json: it can contain API keys and local folder paths. For command-line profile selection and one-run overrides, see Running from the Terminal.

items.title: Running from the Terminal
items.text:
Open your system terminal, then run finagent --terminal.

The packaged finagent command can open the dashboard, run processing without the browser, select a profile, and perform maintenance. On macOS, create the alias described in Install on macOS first.

items.title: Launch and setup
items.text:
Command Behavior finagent Open the dashboard using the Personal profile. finagent --terminal Open the numbered interactive terminal menu. finagent --dashboard-only Start the dashboard without processing. finagent --pipeline-only Process and update dashboard data without starting another dashboard server. finagent --calculation-only Process without starting the dashboard. finagent --no-dashboard Alias for --calculation-only. finagent --setup Run the interactive setup wizard, then optionally open Import. finagent --reconfigure Alias for --setup. finagent --version Print the installed version. finagent --help or -h Print pipeline argument help.

With no arguments, FinAgent opens the existing dashboard and does not reprocess. The Process page starts normal dashboard runs.

items.title: Select a profile
items.text:
--profile may precede any launch, processing, or maintenance command:

finagent --profile personal
finagent --profile dev
finagent --profile dev --orgs boa
finagent --profile=dev --dashboard-only

Personal and Dev are the supported user-facing profiles. See Profiles for isolation and activation behavior.

items.title: Pipeline filters
items.text:
Option Example Purpose --orgs --orgs boa,amex,chase Process only comma-separated institution IDs. --month --month 2026-05 Process one calendar month. --start-date --start-date 2026-01-01 Inclusive start date; YYYYMMDD also works. --end-date --end-date 2026-06-30 Inclusive end date; YYYYMMDD also works. --clean-data --clean-data Delete generated temp and transaction output before the run.

Examples:

finagent --orgs boa,amex
finagent --month 2026-05
finagent --start-date 2026-01-01 --end-date 2026-06-30
finagent --clean-data --orgs boa

When processing also updates the dashboard, a selected date range becomes the inclusive dashboard view without deleting older rows from the persistent master.

items.title: Location Engine options
items.text:
Option Purpose --no-location-lookup Skip location categorization for this run. --lookup-method nominatim Override the run with OpenStreetMap. --lookup-method google_maps Override with Dev Selenium lookup. --lookup-method combined Try OpenStreetMap, then Dev Selenium lookup. --lookup-method place_api Override with Google Places API lookup. --lookup-method place_api_combined Try OpenStreetMap, then Google Places API. --clear-lookup-cache Delete the active method's cache before processing. --refresh-lookup-cache Ignore cached values and replace them with fresh lookups.

See Location Engine before selecting a method that uses an external service.

items.title: Model options
items.text:
Option Purpose --llm-provider ollama Use the local Ollama provider for this run. --llm-provider open_router Use the configured OpenRouter model and key. --llm-provider claude Use the configured Claude model and key. --no-llm Skip model categorization but still write final output. --llm-batch-size NUMBER Override descriptions sent per model request. --clear-llm-cache Delete the active model's categorization cache first. --refresh-llm-cache Rebuild the active model's cache from scratch.

Use --no-llm for a deterministic-only run; none is a saved Settings value, not a valid --llm-provider argument. See AI Engine for provider installation and behavior.

items.title: Diagnostic commands
items.text:
finagent --lookup-method place_api \
  --test-location-lookup "COFFEE SHOP BOSTON MA"

finagent --test-open-router --open-router-config-only
finagent --test-open-router

--test-location-lookup DESCRIPTION runs one merchant through the selected resolver and exits. --test-open-router validates configuration and makes one minimal API request; adding --open-router-config-only skips the network call.

items.title: Non-interactive merge controls
items.text:
These switches accompany --pipeline-only, which is also how the dashboard server starts a background processing run:

Option Purpose --overwrite-user-defined Allow new output to replace prior manual categories. --overwrite-llm Allow new output to replace prior model categories. --overwrite-location Allow new output to replace prior location categories.

Without an overwrite switch, that category source remains protected during the merge.

finagent --pipeline-only --overwrite-llm --overwrite-location

items.title: Cloud API keys
items.text:
Keys saved in Settings or finagent --setup are loaded from the active profile. For a temporary shell-only provider choice, set the matching environment variable before launching.

macOS / LinuxWindows PowerShell 
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="sk-or-your-key"
finagent --llm-provider open_router --orgs boa

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-your-key"
finagent --llm-provider claude --orgs boa

$env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY = "sk-or-your-key"
finagent --llm-provider open_router --orgs boa

$env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "sk-ant-your-key"
finagent --llm-provider claude --orgs boa

Avoid typing secrets directly into commands that shell history may save.

items.title: Dashboard data maintenance
items.text:
Command Behavior finagent --overwrite-dashboard-data Rebuild the dashboard master from the latest pipeline output. finagent --delete-dashboard-data Delete only the dashboard transaction master after confirmation. finagent --reset-all Reset configuration and generated data after confirmation. finagent --reset-all --with-statements Also delete raw statements during the reset. --yes or -y Accept supported confirmation prompts non-interactively.

These operations are intentionally separate from a normal Process run. Back up local data before a reset.

items.title: Dashboard-only date view
items.text:
finagent --dashboard-only \
  --start-date 2026-01-01 \
  --end-date 2026-03-31

This opens a restricted inclusive view without processing or deleting older master transactions.

items.title: No statements available
items.text: A terminal processing request with no statement files opens the dashboard on Import instead of running an empty pipeline. Import a supported CSV or tabular Bank of America checking export, then run the command again.
